rows.note: Use this for liquid tears produced by crying or eye irritation.

example.english: I tear up whenever I cut onions.
example.traditional: 切洋蔥嗰陣，我啲眼淚流個不停。
example.jyutping: cit3 joeng4 cung1 go2 zan6 ngo5 di1 ngaan5 leoi6 lau4 go3 bat1 ting4

rows.note: Use this for ripping material apart, and with the material as subject it also means that it has become torn.

example.english: The paper was so thin that it was easy to tear and got torn.
example.traditional: 張紙太薄，好容易扯爛咗。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 zi2 taai3 bok6 hou2 jung4 ji6 ce2 laan6 zo2

rows.note: Use this for a visible hole or tear in clothing or another material.

example.english: There’s a tear in this shirt, so take it to be mended.
example.traditional: 呢件衫爛咗個窿，快啲拎去補啦。
example.jyutping: ni1 gin6 saam1 laan6 zo2 go3 lung1 faai3 di1 ling1 heoi3 bou2 laa1

rows.note: Use this when forcefully tearing something open or creating an opening in it.

example.english: I tear open the envelope with force.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 lik6 si1 hoi1 go3 seon3 fung1

rows.note: Use this when removing a coupon, page, or other attached piece by tearing it out.

example.english: Tear the coupon out along the dotted line.
example.traditional: 你沿住條虛線將張優惠券撕出嚟。
example.jyutping: nei5 jyun4 zyu6 tiu4 heoi1 sin3 zoeng1 zoeng1 jau1 wai6 gyun3 si1 ceot1 lei4

rows.note: Use this for taking down or demolishing a building or structure.

example.english: They will tear down this old building next month.
example.jyutping: ni1 dung6 gau6 lau4 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 caak3
